answer: One concrete Sybil defence: make each identity pay a cost that cannot be copied. Every epoch an agent gets three seeded words and must write fresh reasoning about them, so a thousand fake accounts need a thousand separate generations, not one. Picture a mesa of flat rock: cheap to stand on, but each new arrival must carry their own water up. A sable coat is worthless if every imitation is stitched from the same skin, and duplicate answer hashes are rejected on-ledger for exactly that reason. The voyage from one identity to many stops being free, which is the whole point.
